title: Upgrade Stripe SDK to v13+ service-based pattern
description:
Upgrade Stripe SDK to v13+ service-based pattern
Stripe SDK v13 introduced a new service-based call pattern through
StripeClient, replacing the resource-based class method approach. The
old pattern (e.g., Stripe::Customer.retrieve) is deprecated and new API
endpoints will only support the service-based approach. We converted all
Stripe::* class methods to client.v1.* service calls

Migration guide:
https://github.com/stripe/stripe-ruby/wiki/Migration-guide-for-v13

Add centralized StripeClient module that provides a cleaner API for
accessing Stripe services. The module delegates method calls to the v1
services, allowing code like: StripeClient.customers.delete(stripe_id)
instead of:
Stripe::StripeClient.new(Config.stripe_secret_key).v1.customers.delete(stripe_id)

We avoid creating a new Stripe::StripeClient per access. Make
StripeClient be the Stripe::V1Services object. In testing, use a Struct
with columns for all v1 services that are used. In addition to being
faster by avoiding indirection, this also makes the mocking code
simpler.

title: Pre create aws subnets per az
description:
## Add aws_subnet table for pre-created AZ subnets
Previously, AWS subnets were created per-NIC at VM provision
time, leading to a proliferation of subnets and hitting AWS
limits. This migration adds an aws_subnet table to track
pre-created subnets, one per availability zone per VPC.

The nic_aws_resource table gains an aws_subnet_id foreign key
to reference which shared subnet each NIC uses.

## Add AwsSubnet model and wire up associations
Introduce the AwsSubnet Sequel model with associations to
PrivateSubnetAwsResource and LocationAwsAz. Update
NicAwsResource and PrivateSubnetAwsResource with the
corresponding reverse associations.

## Pre-create one AWS subnet per AZ at VPC creation time
Instead of creating subnets on-demand per NIC, SubnetNexus
now pre-allocates AwsSubnet records (one per AZ) with IPv4
CIDRs during assembly. VpcNexus then materializes them as
actual AWS subnets once the VPC and its IPv6 block are
available.

The destroy path gains a delete_az_subnets label. On VPC
deletion, DependencyViolation is re-raised for strand retry
rather than looping back explicitly.

## Allocate NICs from pre-created AZ subnets
NicNexus.assemble now selects an AwsSubnet at assembly time
based on the requested availability zone, and allocates an
IPv4 address from that subnet's CIDR (respecting the five
AWS-reserved addresses). The chosen subnet ID is stored in
the strand frame.

Aws::NicNexus no longer creates or manages per-NIC subnets
for new VPCs. Legacy per-NIC subnets are still deleted during
NIC teardown; shared AZ subnets are left for VPC cleanup.

## Add backfill prog for existing VPCs
BackfillAwsSubnets is a one-shot prog that migrates VPCs
created before the per-AZ subnet architecture. It handles
two cases:

- /26 VPCs (legacy): discovers the single existing subnet
  and creates one AwsSubnet record
- /16 VPCs (current): inventories existing per-NIC subnets,
  groups them by AZ, creates AwsSubnet records, then
  provisions new AWS subnets for any uncovered AZs

In both cases it links existing NICs to the appropriate
AwsSubnet via nic_aws_resource.aws_subnet_id.

## Update unrelated specs for SubnetNexus.assemble changes
SubnetNexus.assemble now creates AwsSubnet records during
assembly, which requires a LocationAwsAz to exist for AWS
locations. Add the necessary AZ setup to specs that assemble
AWS subnets indirectly.

## Support dynamic AWS subnet sizing based on VPC range
Pass ipv4_range_size to create_aws_subnet_records so AZ subnets can be
sized relative to the VPC. The subnet prefix is calculated as
min(vpc_size + 8, 28) to respect AWS's /28 minimum subnet size.

Handle edge cases where the VPC is too small:
- If VPC prefix equals subnet prefix, force single-AZ mode and use the
  entire VPC as the subnet
- If VPC is smaller than /28, raise an error since AWS doesn't allow
  subnets smaller than /28
- If VPC can't fit all AZs, log a warning and skip the extra AZs

## Limit GitHub runner VPCs to a single AZ subnet
GitHub runners are ephemeral single-VM workloads that do not
need subnets pre-created in every availability zone. Pass
limit_to_single_az to SubnetNexus.assemble so only one
randomly chosen AZ gets an AwsSubnet record, reducing
unnecessary AWS resource creation.

## Switch from limit_to_single_az to preferred_azs
Instead of passing a flag to only ask for a single az, the caller can
specify their preferred azs. This way, if the ask is a single az, they
can list a single az. This was a better design because the github
runners were excluding the az "a" and preferred a single az. Instead of
introducing multiple flags to the prog for the same job, I decided to
use preferred_azs.

title: Support Stop and Start for VMs
description:
In addition to supporting stop and start for VMs, this has a number of other related changes:

* Restart semaphore now has an effect when VM is in unavailable state
* Restart (and start/stop) results in an error for AWS VMs (better than silently accepted and ignoring)
* Restart (and start/stop) results in an error if the metal VM is not in an expected state
* Show unavailable as a display state for VMs
* Do not page when a VM becomes unavailable, as the most likely case is the user shut it down from inside the VM
* Add unavailable VMs page to admin site, so admins can see which VMs are unavailable (now that it doesn't page)

Not paging for unavailable VMs is probably the most controversial change here. I'm not opposed to paging for unavailable VMs if we know for sure that the unavailability is due to a problem that an admin can fix. However, as long as the unavailability is caused by customer action and out of the admin's control, I don't think we should page for it. Blindly restarting the VMs to address the page is generally the wrong solution, because the user may have shut down the VM for security or other reasons. With this change, the user can start the VM if they have shut it down, via the web or the API/CLI.

title: Destroy child strands when entering pg lockout
description:
When entering lockout, destroy any existing child strands to prevent
them from blocking the reap in wait_lockout_attempt.

The specific scenario: a restart strand was stuck as a child due to
unavailability, which blocked the reap and caused infinite wait. Since
lockout is about to stop primary, no in-flight child operations
(restart, configure, etc.) should be necessary.

title: Run metal and AWS E2E tests in parallel
description:
As we introduce new tests, the overall E2E runtime keeps increasing. To mitigate this, we can run the metal and aws E2E tests in parallel.

The biggest challenge here is runner tests. Since they share the same GitHub App, it’s not possible to run them in parallel within the same repository.

To solve this, I created two separate GitHub Apps (e2e-test-app-metal, e2e-test-app-aws) and two repositories (tahcloud/github-e2e-tests-metal, tahcloud/github-e2e-tests-aws) so the tests can run in parallel.

I added configurations for these into two separate environments in this repository (E2E-metal, E2E-aws). Each job uses its own environment to access the correct secrets.

The changes in the runner test prog are a bit ugly. I have another branch to simplify it.

Previously, when we ran the tests serially, if the metal tests failed, the AWS tests wouldn’t even start. Now, even if the metal tests are broken, we can still see the AWS results.

Since most of the time is spent on the metal tests, they take ~56m, while the AWS tests take ~8m. This doesn’t significantly affect the overall runtime, but it gives us ~48m of free time to add more tests for the AWS provider.

title: Add cluster level monitoring to UbiCSI node-plugin daemonset
description:
**Add Mesh Connectivity Monitoring to Kubernetes CSI**
This PR implements mesh network connectivity monitoring for Kubernetes clusters, enabling detection of network isolation between pods and external endpoints.

**Changes**
**Mesh Connectivity Checker**

- Add MeshConnectivityChecker that runs as a background thread in the CSI node plugin
- Periodically verify TCP connectivity to other pods in all other nodes on certain intervals
- Support external endpoint monitoring via EXTERNAL_ENDPOINTS environment variable
- Write connectivity status to /var/lib/ubicsi/mesh_status.json using atomic file writes

**KubernetesNode Health Monitoring**

- Integrate KubernetesNode into the central health monitor system
- Read mesh status file via SSH and report node as down if any peer is unreachable
- Include external endpoint reachability in health checks

**Infrastructure**

- Remove hostNetwork: true from CSI DaemonSet to validate actual CNI network paths
- Add network debugging tools to CSI Docker image (netcat, mtr, traceroute, etc.)
**Refactor** 
- yaml_load_kubectl to automatically append -oyaml

description:
We have been seeing issues related to Kubernetes clusters
    having connectivity issues, therefore we aim to set periodic
    checks for specific clusters and get alerted for
    timely investigation.

We utilize the connectivity_check_target column in kubernetes_cluster
    by running checks from each node.

A `cluster_health_report` method that verifies external connectivity
    from each node's ubicsi-nodeplugin pod is added.

When configured, the wait loop runs the check every 2 minutes
    and pages on failure.

This check is planned to be moved to ubicsi plugin in the future.

title: Introduce configurable subnet size
description:
## Add ipv4_range_size parameter to SubnetNexus.assemble
This allows callers to specify a custom IPv4 CIDR prefix length
when assembling a subnet, falling back to the existing defaults
for AWS and non-AWS locations when not specified.

## Cap AWS subnet CIDR to match private subnet prefix length
When creating an AWS subnet in NicNexus, use the private subnet's
actual prefix length (capped at /24) instead of always using /24.
This ensures that subnets with smaller ranges (e.g. /28) get
correctly sized AWS subnets.

## Use /28 subnet size for GitHub runner subnets
GitHub runners create a high volume of subnets which causes CIDR
conflicts with the default /16 range. Reduce the subnet size to
/28, the smallest allowed by AWS, to minimize address space
consumption and avoid conflicts.

title: Connection Checkout Metrics Changes
description:
* Allow for separate web/respirate pool size. This will allow for decreasing the web pool size in production.
* Adjust the buckets, since the <10ms buckets aren't useful in production.
* Report more often (20s instead of 60s), to ensure smooth metric graphs
* Remove respirate checkout metrics (since none are emitted)

title: Disable RSpec/ExpectChange cop
description:
It recommends changing:

```
change { nx.stop_set? }.from(false).to(true)
```

to:

```
change(nx, :stop_set?)
```

which loses the direction of the change.

title: Fix 2 N+1 query issues in Vm serializer detailed view
description: In detailed view, the VM serialier includes firewall information, which results in N+1 queries to get the location and firewall rules for each firewall. Eager load those to fix the issue.

title: Support phasing initial resource load in monitor
description:
Previously, when monitor started up, it would immediately queue up
all of its resources. In production, that can result in over 1000
threads competing for only 60 database connections, which led to pool
timeouts on startup. This phases the initial load over the first third
of the scan period, or over the first 20 seconds by default. So if
there are 1000 resources to monitor, it will load them up about 50 per
second for the first 20 seconds.

Because of how the run_queue works, this has the effect that the first
resources to monitor won't be monitored again until after 20 seconds,
which goes against the design the tries to monitor them 5 seconds
after monitoring last finished. However, after the first 20 seconds,
the program goes into steady state. I think this is a reasonable
trade-off to avoid pool timeouts at monitor startup.

Bet reviewed ignoring whitespace.

title: Fix stale pods accumulating in mesh connectivity status
description:
Pods deleted from the cluster (via scaling, rolling updates, or node removal) were never removed from @pod_status, causing mesh_status.json to grow indefinitely with non-existent pods and failing health checks.

After each connectivity check cycle, prune entries for pods that are no longer returned by the Kubernetes API.

Implement the checkup mechanism for KubernetesNode to create pages when mesh connectivity issues persist.

When a node is down for 5+ consecutive readings over 15 minutes, it triggers a checkup.

description: Without this, old DNS records are not deleted, and you can end up with duplicate `private.` DNS records, which is definitely not desirable as only one should be valid.

title: Do not cc the support email for invoice failures
description:
Previously, cc’ing the support email was helpful for visibility when customers created support tickets about failed invoice payments.

However, now that we have an admin panel, anyone can easily check invoice statuses there.

We can remove the support email from cc on invoice failures, as it no longer adds value and mostly creates noise.

title: Use dynamic CIDR prefix in CNI IPv4 setup
description: Replace hardcoded /24 prefix with dynamic prefix extracted from the subnet configuration. The prefix is now derived from the subnet_ipv4 input parameter, allowing the CNI to work correctly with any subnet size (e.g., /24, /26).

title: PostgreSQL Auto Scale Up
description:
**Remove unused unlock function**
I found this while adding the decr_ helper methods for models. This is
left over from the old implementation and we stopped using it as part of
avoiding N+1 queries. All its old callers now use Semaphore.where(...)

**Use decr helper instead of deleting semaphores directly**
I found this while adding the decr helper function for models. In this
case, it is used in a prog, so it alrready has its own decr_ function.

**Add decr_ helper methods for models**
We have a similar helper method for incrementing semaphores, but we
don't have a helper method for decrementing them. This commit adds decr_
helper methods for models that use semaphores, allowing us to easily
decrement semaphores.

**Move generate_postgres_options to PostgresResource model**
We need to use `generate_postgres_options` in respirate as well. At the
moment, it is only available in we Clover app. Moving it to the model
allows us to reuse it in respirate and other parts of the system.

**Add automatic storage scaling for PostgreSQL databases**
Automatically scale up PostgreSQL storage when disk usage reaches
critical thresholds. The system monitors disk usage and takes
progressive action:
- At 80% and 85%: sends warning emails to project owners with
  details about the upcoming auto-scale
- At 90%: triggers auto-scaling by updating target storage size
  (and VM size if needed), including read replicas.

**Allow users to cancel in-progress storage auto-scale**
We use advisory locks to prevent race conditions with ongoing converge
operations. Users can cancel from the settings page while the operation
is in early stages (start, provision_servers, wait_servers_to_be_ready).

When canceled, target sizes are reset to current values, a notification
email is sent warning about potential unavailability at 100% usage. We
also create a page to notify on-call.

title: Add usage summary to GitHub runner dashboard
description: Users currently lack clear visibility into their runner usage and associated costs. This change adds a summary section to the GitHub runner dashboard that shows allocated vCPUs, requested vCPUs, today's cost, and the cost over the last 30 days. When customers have hundreds of runners, it's easy to lose track of how many vCPUs are allocated versus requested. Some customers already run over 1,000 vCPUs concurrently, but this effectively unlimited concurrency isn't visible or communicated anywhere today. It advertises our ability to support very high concurrency and scale beyond typical limits. While historical data would also be valuable, this is a good first step toward improving visibility.

title: Add knotc telemetry
description:
Per comment, stdin is useful as it's faster than forking many knotc commands, in spite of the difficulty aligning and matching error output.

However, per recent incident, it's probably not too voluminous to record.  We could have reacted far faster and learned a lot more with materialized copies of what was done, and when.

title: Redesign GitHub runner empty state for better onboarding
description: The previous empty state was a plain text block that didn't match the app's standard empty state pattern and buried the setup steps in a paragraph. New users had to parse a wall of text to figure out how to get started. Replace it with a structured layout that follows the app's empty state conventions: centered icon, title, numbered step cards, and a primary CTA button. Add a secondary banner to surface runner options (more vCPU, arm64, premium) with a link to the runner types documentation. Also add the hero-rocket-launch icon to the icon set. title: Fix nondeterministic dns zone modifiction in Prog::DnsZone::DnsZoneNexus
description:
For records with the same created_at, remove any tombstoned records before adding new records. Otherwise, we can add a record and then remove it.

Progs that both delete_record and insert_record in the same label (same transaction) use delete_record first, so the intent is to update the data for the record, not delete the record.

title: Support Ubiblk v0.2.2.
description:
This version fixes an issue which caused qemu VMs fail to boot. With v0.2.1, qemu boot errored out with:

```
Reconnecting after error: Received bad msg size.
```

This was because unlike cloud-hypervisor, qemu requested a prefix of virtio-block config, but ubiblk returned the omplete 60 byte config regardless of the requested size.

This was fixed in https://github.com/ubicloud/ubiblk/commit/e807644fc987d4f1bc8b5ee50e6f30786ff43ffe

Since this is basically v0.2.1 + the fix, we are removing v0.2.1 support for future installations.

title: Persist firewall rules on Kubernetes nodes across reboots
description:
Replaces the previous approach of applying iptables and nft rules at runtime with writing a complete nftables ruleset to /etc/nftables.conf and enabling the nftables systemd service. This ensures NAT masquerading and IPv6 pod access control rules survive node reboots.

The ruleset includes a flush to start clean, an ip nat table for POSTROUTING masquerade, and an ip6 pod_access table for ingress and egress filtering.

title: Add stack trace to mesh checker
description:
Include stack trace in mesh connectivity error reports

Previously, error strings in initiate_connection and check_socket_error only included the exception class and message. This made it difficult to diagnose connectivity failures from the status report. Now the full backtrace is appended to the error string, providing the call chain context needed for debugging.

title: Spread out retries when facing AWS instance restrictions
description: Retrying quickly leads to multiple create/delete EIP calls, especially when AWS does not have capacity leading to abuse warning from AWS. This spaces the retries to 5 minutes post excluded_azs reset

description:
Extract the following private methods:

* handle_storage_auto_scale_action(disk_usage_percent)
* cancel_storage_auto_scale_action(disk_usage_percent)
* perform_storage_auto_scale_action(disk_usage_percent)

title: Add Overrider
description:
Overrider is designed to make it easier for people to build on top of Ubicloud and avoid merge conflicts.

Without this, typical behavior for people building on top of Ubicloud would be to modify the code they want to change directly. However, that will often result in merge conflicts later if we modify the same code location.

With Overrider, the overrides are placed in files in a separate directory, and are prepended to the classes to override the default behavior (can call super to get the default behavior).

Overrider is designed to handle only classes/modules defined inside the repository. It ignores other classes/modules as well as any anonymous classes/modules. Loading it into a superclass before subclassing will automatically load overrides for subclasses when those subclasses are created. This allows for overrides to work properly when using incremental testing.

Ubicloud doesn't use Overrider itself except during unfrozen testing, where it uses it for all models and progs (though only a single model is overridden with some test methods).

title: Fix billing rate setup for hobby instances
Prevent immediate reconvergence due to pruning servers
description: At the prune_servers label, we increment destroy semaphore for servers to be destroyed, but we don't wait for them to be actually destroyed. Then PostgresResource detects extra servers and realizes it is not converged (having more servers than desired), and starts reconvergence immediately. This commit adds a new label wait_prune_servers after prune_servers to wait until servers to be destroyed are actually destroyed.

title: Ensure representative_server is never nil
description:
representative_server of a resource is defined as the server which has
its representative_at value set. The ideal place to be would be having
one and only one representative_server for a resource for the entire
lifetime of the resource. "Only one" part is guaranteed by the UNIQUE
constraint on the database level. "One" part is not guaranteed, because
representative_server can be nil during failovers.

To prevent representative_server from being nil, we need to hand over
being representative_server in a single transaction. In the current form
this is not possible, because destruction of old primary and promotion
of new primary is done by separate strands.

To bring both these operations into the same transaction, we need to
decouple representative_server handover from the destruction of the old
primary. For this purpose, we are adding a new database column called
is_representative. Now during standby promotion, we can both unset the
is_representative of the old primary and set the is_representative of
new primary. Actual destruction of the old primary is done after that.

However, there is one important implication of keeping the old primary
around for a while. During failover, we need to make sure that the old
primary is fenced. This is not a problem for planned failovers, because
we can still access to the old primary and fence it from the inside of
the VM. For unplanned failovers, it is partly OK as well, because for
unplanned failovers, the expectation is that the old primary is already
down, so there is no need to fence. However, if the old primary is not
really down for example, due to a network partition or false positive,
then keeping it around for a while can cause split brain. To prevent
this, we still try to lockout the old primary but it is not guaranteed
to work.

That said, this is not a new defect, because even in the current form,
we don't wait underlying VM to be destroyed, so there is still risk of
split brain if the old primary is not really down. I'm working on a more
general fix for this problem. This change, doesn't change the state of
the defect, but gives us stable invariant that representative_server is
never nil.

Add mtr check to mesh checker
description:
**Add on-demand MTR diagnostics to mesh connectivity checker**
When intermittent connectivity issues occur between Kubernetes nodes, simple reachability checks tell us a pod is unreachable but not where in the network path the problem lies. This PR adds failure-triggered MTR diagnostics that automatically run when connectivity checks fail, providing hop-by-hop network visibility.

**On-demand MTR**: When a pod connectivity check fails, MTR runs against the failed pod IP. For external endpoints, DNS resolution failures trigger MTR against CoreDNS pod IPs, while connection errors trigger MTR against the endpoint directly. MTR targets are processed through a background queue that blocks until work arrives. Results are cleared automatically when targets recover, and stale entries for removed pods are pruned each cycle.

**Configurable log level**: The mesh checker runs kubectl commands every 30 seconds to discover pods, generating redundant info-level log noise. A log level parameter on the Kubernetes client (defaulting to info) lets the mesh checker demote these to debug.

**API server error reporting**: Previously, if the API server became unreachable, the status file retained the last known healthy state - giving a false impression that everything was fine. The checker now records the API error with backtrace in the status file and clears it once the API recovers. The node availability check treats the API error as unavailable, surfacing it through Clog emissions.

**MTR results in availability checks**: MTR results are included in the availability result hash when connectivity issues are detected, making network path data available in Clog emissions. They are informational and do not affect the availability decision.

title: Add stop action for vm in admin panel
Fix csi upgrade incompatibility
description:
**Wait for CSI data copy before removing Kubernetes nodes**
**Problem**
When a Kubernetes node is retired (upgrade or nodepool resize), the CSI driver starts a background rsync to copy persistent volume data from the old node to the new one. Previously, the node nexus proceeded directly from drain to node removal, destroying the VM while the copy was potentially still in progress. Since rsync reads from the old node over SSH, this caused irreversible data loss.

**Solution**
Added a wait_for_copy label in KubernetesNodeNexus between drain and remove_node_from_cluster. It queries all PersistentVolumes for the old-pvc-object annotation with nodeAffinity pointing to the retiring node. While such PVs exist, the nexus naps and rechecks every 15 seconds. The node remains visible in the cluster during the wait for debuggability.

**E2E Test**
Added an end-to-end test that retires a node hosting a StatefulSet pod and verifies:

- The node is not removed while PVs still reference it for data migration
- Data integrity is preserved after the copy completes via sha256sum comparison


**Changes**
- New wait_for_copy label in the node nexus, drain hops to it on success
- Three new e2e test labels: test_node_not_deleted_during_copy, verify_node_not_deleted_during_copy, verify_data_after_drain
- Unit tests for wait_for_copy
- Specs for the new e2e test labels, refactored subject to include kubernetes_cluster_id in the strand stack

title: Fix custom label active runner issues
description:
- **Exclude apply_custom_label_quota label when calculating active runner vCPUs**
  When calculating the active runner vCPUs for a project, we exclude
  runner labels where the VM has not yet been allocated. In these cases,
  the runner may already be waiting on that label due to concurrency
  limits.
  
  We recently added the apply_custom_label_quota label for the custom
  label feature, but it was not included in the excluded labels list. As a
  result, runners waiting on the custom label quota are incorrectly
  counted as active runners, even though no VM has been allocated yet.
  
  We should ensure that any label applied before VM allocation is included
  in the excluded labels list.
  

- **Show custom label quota status on active runners page**
  Runners waiting in the apply_custom_label_quota step had no
  dedicated status message and fell through to the generic
  "Provisioning an ephemeral virtual machine" text. This was
  misleading because the runner is actually waiting for a custom
  label concurrency slot, not provisioning a VM.

title: Fix missing DNS records when adding ports to load balancer
description:
LoadBalancer#add_port and #remove_port were the only mutation methods
that did not call incr_rewrite_dns_records. This caused a race
condition during Kubernetes LoadBalancer service creation:
sync_kubernetes_services calls add_vm (which sets rewrite_dns_records)
before add_port, but since the services LB starts with zero ports,
add_vm creates zero LoadBalancerVmPort entries. If the LB nexus strand
processes rewrite_dns_records before add_port runs, vms_to_dns returns
empty (the join through load_balancer_vm_port finds nothing), so DNS
records are deleted and never recreated — add_port only set
update_load_balancer, not rewrite_dns_records.

Adding incr_rewrite_dns_records to both add_port and remove_port
ensures DNS records are rewritten after port changes, matching the
behavior of add_vm, remove_vm, evacuate_vm, and remove_vm_port.

title: Remove storage volume `skip_sync`.
description:
We originally introduced `skip_sync` during the SPDK-only phase to make flush I/O requests no-ops on GitHub runners, where durability across VM crashes or host reboots was not required. This worked because SPDK used a single I/O thread per VM, avoiding concurrency concerns.

With ubiblk (multi-threaded I/O), skipping flushes was not as simple as turning them into no-ops and led to correctness issues (notably in ubiblk v0.1.7). Since the feature provided limited practical value and increased maintenance complexity, we removed it from ubiblk in December 2025.

We no longer operate SPDK-based GitHub runner hosts, so `skip_sync` can also be removed from Ubicloud.

**Notes:**

1. This change updates both Clover and Rhizome in the same commit. This is safe because, the previous rhizome implementation defaults to false if the field is absent.
2. On the database side: `vm_storage_volume.skip_sync` and `vm_pool.storage_skip_sync` both default to false, so removing them will just put an ignored value of false in those tables. Database column removals will be handled in a separate migration PR.

title: Add PostgresResource and PostgresServer tables to admin panel
description:
### Skip eager loading on Vm when fetched as an association

AutoForme's :eager option runs every time a record is fetched, not
just on the listing page. PostgresServer eagerly loads [:resource,
:vm], and Vm eagerly loads [:location, :vm_host, :project]. Since
PostgresResource also eagerly loads [:project, :location, :parent],
visiting the PostgresServer list causes duplicate project and location
queries through both associations.

AutoForme supports a block form for :eager that receives the fetch
type, similar to Rodauth's per-request configuration. When a Vm is
fetched as an association (type == :association), the display only
needs name or ubid, so skip the eager loads in that case.

title: Allow to run pry in E2E runner
description:
- **Allow SSH access to the E2E test runner**
  This lets us use pry while the E2E tests are running.
  

- **Persist essential env vars to .env.rb in E2E workflow**
  Environment variables set in the step-level `env:` block are not
  available when SSH-ing into the runner for debugging. This makes it
  impossible to start a pry session, as .env.rb lacks the database URL,
  rack environment, and service project IDs needed to boot the app.
  
  Move CLOVER_DATABASE_URL, RACK_ENV, IS_E2E, and the service project
  ID variables out of `env:` and write them directly into .env.rb in a
  dedicated step. This way, an operator who connects via SSH can start
  pry and run queries:
  
      cd work/ubicloud/ubicloud
      /opt/hostedtoolcache/Ruby/3.4.8/x64/bin/ruby ./bin/pry
  
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
  

- **Allow pry without INGEST_KEY in E2E environment**
  The E2E runner uses RACK_ENV=production to stay close to prod, but
  it does not have an INGEST_KEY. This blocks operators from starting
  pry when SSH-ing into the runner for debugging.
  
  Skip the INGEST_KEY check when Config.is_e2e is set, since audit
  logging is not needed in the E2E environment.
  
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: Fix AWS private subnet leak on insufficient capacity
description:
When an AWS instance lacks capacity, the runner is destroyed and a spare is provisioned. Previously, we also triggered vm.incr_destroy alongside runner.incr_destroy. Because the VM prog (Vm::Aws::Nexus) now manages the AWS instance directly, unlike the old separate Aws::Instance prog, destroying the VM before the GitHub runner processes its cleanup causes the runner to skip private subnet teardown, leaving it orphaned.

Remove the redundant vm.incr_destroy call so that the GitHub runner nexus handles the full teardown sequence, including the private subnet:

https://github.com/ubicloud/ubicloud/blob/7fe14dc95/prog/github/github_runner_nexus.rb#L534-L544

Also extend the nap from 0 to 60 seconds, giving the current runner time to clean up before retrying.

title: Fix N+1 issues on Vm/PrivateSubnet index pages
Handle already deleted API tokens when destroying cache entries
description:
Cache entry cleanup involves both a database deletion and blob storage operations (abort multipart upload, delete object). If a previous attempt partially succeeds, deleting the bucket or API token but failing to commit the database change, the retry will encounter errors from the storage client.

The existing rescue for Aws::S3::Errors::NoSuchKey handles the case where the blob was already removed. Add Aws::S3::Errors::Unauthorized to also handle the case where the API token has already been revoked.

title: Add provider selection to /run-e2e PR comment trigger
description:
The E2E workflow already supports a providers input for choosing which providers to run against, but the /run-e2e comment trigger only exposed the test_cases argument. This meant contributors had to use the GitHub UI to trigger provider-scoped runs.

The comment syntax is now `/run-e2e [providers] [test_cases]`, e.g. `/run-e2e metal vm,postgres_ha`. Both arguments remain optional and are validated with the same alphanumeric pattern.

title: Add stop-vm action to rhizome
description:
This will do a nice stop on the VM, giving the VM a chance to shutdown normally. It currently only works with cloud-hypervisor VMs.

This is the first commit in #4791, but pushing a separate PR for this so it can be included with an upcoming rhizome rollout.

title: Support JSON log format in cache proxy telemetry collection
description:
- **Simplify cache proxy log processing in telemetry collection**
  The previous implementation iterated the log lines four times: strip,
  select, gsub, and tally+emit. Consolidate into a single each_line loop
  that strips, filters, sanitizes, and emits in one pass.
  
  Also remove the tally step so each matching line is emitted individually
  rather than grouped with a count, and use a regex for the 204 status
  code check to handle varying whitespace.
  

- **Support JSON log format in cache proxy telemetry collection**
  The new version of cache proxy prints logs in JSON format, which is more
  structured and easier to parse. Our monitoring system can now easily
  extract relevant information from the logs and we can query them easily.
  
  It's expected to get 204 and 409 errors from cache backend, so no need
  to log them as errors.

This allows us to connect to the E2E host while tests are running and debug them if needed, without any manual work.

The only tricky part is that the keys in
`secrets.OPERATOR_SSH_PUBLIC_KEYS` must be separated by `\r\n`. Using just `\n` is not sufficient for a YAML multiline string.

title: Quote MAC addresses in cloud-init network-config YAML
description:
https://github.com/ubicloud/ubicloud/commit/60427ce920a793bdbc845827abfd0d79a2d76c2f switched cloud-init config generation from heredoc string
interpolation to YAML.dump.  This lost the explicit double-quoting
on MAC addresses that was added in https://github.com/ubicloud/ubicloud/pull/746 to fix a YAML 1.1
compatibility issue.

Ruby's Psych emits colon-separated all-numeric values like
"12:40:37:27:57:41" unquoted, because YAML 1.2 has no sexagesimal
type.  Cloud-init uses Python's PyYAML, which defaults to YAML 1.1
and parses these as base-60 integers.  When the VM happens to
receive a MAC where every octet is purely numeric and <=59, PyYAML
converts it to an integer, the interface match fails, and the guest
never requests a DHCP lease.

Post-process the YAML.dump output to force double-quoting on MAC
address values so cloud-init always receives a string.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: Limit alien VM provisioning to runners with 16 or fewer vCPUs
description:
We provision 30–60 vCPUs instead of 32–64 vCPUs for allocation reasons.

With 30 vCPUs, the size calculation (30 / 4) results in a 7xlarge instance type, which AWS doesn’t support. We could round this up to 8xlarge (32 vCPUs), but spot instances of that size aren’t always available.

For now, we should provision alien runners only for smaller runner sizes.

Introduce a support_alien? helper that restricts both the random alien ratio path and the spill-over path to x64 runners with at most 16 vCPUs.

title: Simplify GitHub runner e2e tests to use a single workflow run
description:
Previously each test case triggered and tracked a separate workflow
(test_2204.yml, test_2404.yml, etc.), complicating the prog with
per-case iteration in trigger, check, and cancel steps. A single
workflow dispatched with the runner labels as an input can spawn
multiple jobs internally, so we only need to track one run.

The test case config no longer carries per-case workflow details; the
prog derives the required runner labels from the test case names and
passes them to the workflow.

Use the new return_run_details parameter in the workflow dispatch API
to get the run ID directly from the response, eliminating the need to
poll workflow runs and search by creation time and name. This removes
the 30-second sleep and the created_at tracking from the stack frame.

https://github.blog/changelog/2026-02-19-workflow-dispatch-api-now-returns-run-ids/

The branch is pinned to "enes/simply-tests" temporarily because the
workflow file on the target repository is not yet on main. It will
be switched to main once existing branches are rebased.

title: Fix strand exception logging
description:
Previously, if a respirate strand raised an exception, it was not caught by Strand#run, it was caught by
Dispatcher#run_strand. Unfortunately, the strand reported by Dispatcher#run_strand may not be the strand that actually caused the error, due to parent strands running child strands in Prog#reap.

Introduce Strand::RunError for wrapping the exceptions. If a strand raises an exception, it will be logged with the strand that actually caused the exception, and then wrapped in RunError and reraised. Parent strands that run child strands that raise RunError pass it through without rewrapping it. Dispatcher no longer logs RunError exceptions, since they have already been logged.

There is a fair amount of internal exceptions raised in Strand and Prog::Base. Use Strand::InternalError instead of RuntimeError for these, and don't wrap those errors. These errors are programming bugs and should never be hit in production code.

Avoid RunError wrapping in pry, as it could complicate debugging.

title: Update to autoforme master branch
description: This is done to support the fallback of model configuration methods to framework configuration methods in the admin site, which DRYs up some code.

title: Add `View in Clover` links to admin panel
description: Useful for redistributors to easily drill down during investigation

title: Support Ubiblk v0.4.0.
description:
Notable changes in ubiblk v0.4.0:

- Archive export & stripe sources
- Remote stripe server & stripe sources
- Security fixes
- ublk backend
- Config v2
- Disk metadata format improvements

Majority of changes in the commit is to support config v2, which is documented at: https://github.com/ubicloud/ubiblk/blob/main/docs/config.md

In config v1, the key encryption key (KEK) path was passed as a command line argument. In v2, it's embedded in the config file instead.

We use the KEK in two places: `init-metadata` and the systemd unit. Previously, `init-metadata` received it via stdin and the systemd unit received it via a named pipe. Since v2 embeds the KEK path in the config file, and we use the same config file for both, we've switched both to use named pipes.

We could have kept stdin for v1's `init-metadata`, but that would mean additional branching in the code. For simplicity, this commit also switches v1 `init-metadata` to named pipes.

Named pipes were chosen over two alternatives:

- stdin: can't easily pass stdin to a systemd unit, and using /dev/shm to materialize it as a file is worse for security (root directory traversal).
- RPC: the current implementation of RPC server starts after device setup, so using it for KEK delivery would require reordering startup, adding complexity for little benefit.

title: Append triggered E2E workflow run URL to the /run-e2e comment
description:
GitHub's workflow dispatch API now supports returning run details via the return_run_details parameter [1]. Use this to get the run URL directly from the response, then edit the original /run-e2e comment to append it. This gives immediate visibility into the triggered run.

[1] https://github.blog/changelog/2026-02-19-workflow-dispatch-api-now-returns-run-ids/

title: Flatten mesh availability output for log compatibility
description:
The integrated log system supports only 3 levels of nesting and a limited number of unique keys. The hash-keyed-by-name structures (pod_errors, external_errors, mtr_results) in check_mesh_availability create unbounded unique keys and deep nesting, which the log system cannot index or query effectively.

Convert these three fields from hashes keyed by target name to arrays with the name stored as a field inside each element. This reduces the nesting depth by one level and eliminates dynamic keys, making the log output compatible with the system's constraints.

title: Add nftables persistence test after VM reboot
description:
After the node drain E2E test, we now reboot a worker node and verify that nftables rules survive the reboot. This catches regressions where firewall rules set up during node provisioning (ip nat for SNAT/DNAT and ip6 pod_access for pod network access) are not persisted and would be lost on reboot.

The test captures the ip nat and ip6 pod_access table output before rebooting, waits for the VM to come back, and compares the rules. A mismatch in either table sets a fail_message.

title: Handle failed rsync during CSI data migration with retry
description:
When daemonizer2 reports a failed rsync copy during volume migration, the old behavior raised a hard error immediately, leaving the daemonizer2 unit in a failed state. Subsequent kubelet retries would see the same stale "Failed" status and never recover — the volume would be stuck permanently.

Now on failure, the daemonizer2 unit is cleaned and a CopyNotFinishedError is raised so kubelet can retry the copy from scratch. A retry counter is persisted as a PV annotation (csi.ubicloud.com/migration-retry-count) so it survives pod restarts. After 3 failed attempts, the unit is left intact for log inspection and a hard error is raised directing the user to contact support. The annotation is cleaned up on successful copy completion.

title: Version tracking for rhizome installations
description:
**Record rhizome info upon installation**
    
    Enhance Prog::InstallRhizome to persist a RhizomeInstallation record.
    These data points are persisted:
    
    - folder: target folder of rhizome installation
    - commit: 8-character git commit hash.
    - digest: 24-character hex digest of rhizome (file path+content).
    - installed_at: Timestamp of successful completion.

**Add RhizomeInstallation model**

**Migration: Add rhizome_installation table**
    
    Separate table associated with sshable to keep track of which version of
    rhizome is currently installed on the sshable resource.

**Add GIT_COMMIT_HASH to environment and Config**
    
    Establish a single source of truth for the current git revision across
    environments and process types (web, monitor, respirate).
    
    - loader.rb: Resolve revision from Heroku , Dokku, or local git.
    - config.rb: Expose the value via Config.git_commit_hash.
    - Standardize on an 8-character short hash

title: Make respirate handle database disconnects
description:
If a disconnect is detected, have the thread sleep for 100ms and retry. Do this for the main (scan) thread, repartition thread, and all worker threads.

If a disconnect error happens in a worker thread, don't add the respirate metric and don't close the apoptosis thread.

title: Guard VM user/group cleanup in create_unix_user
description:
The old `userdel --remove --force || true` and `groupdel -f || true` suppress all errors to achieve idempotency.  This masks real problems: -f silently kills lingering processes or removes groups with other members, and || true swallows permission and I/O errors.

Replace with explicit guards: check `id`/`getent group` before removal, terminate lingering processes with logged output, and drop -f from both commands.  Failures now propagate and the control plane retries with backoff until the host is clean.

title: Combine monitoring of Vm and VmHostSlice into VmHost monitoring
description:
This allows Vm and VmHostSlice to share the SSH connection that the VmHost uses for monitoring. It also reduces the number of monitor jobs, since the VmHost job also monitors all Vms and VmHostSlices on the VmHost.

This attempts to support this with minimal changes. Vm and VmHostSlice are each individually wrapped in MonitorableResources, and their check_pulse methods remain the same.  There are two main changes

MonitorResourceType#scan when setup for this support will scan for the Vms and VmHostSlices related to hosts in the current partition. This changes behavior from behavior, where the monitor process monitored Vms and VmHostSlices in the current partition.  This is some complexity here due to having to deal with new and removed resources.

MonitorableResource#check_pulse is monitored in two ways. First, if there is an exception, it checks whether the resource still exists, and marks it as deleted if not. Second, after checking the pulse for the current resource, it will check the pulse for attached resources, removing any that no longer exist.

The {Vm,VmHostSlice}#init_health_monitor_session methods are removed as the session is now created by the VmHost.

title: Exclude GitHub runner slices from health monitoring
description: Runner VMs are already excluded from monitor_models via `.exclude(unix_user: "runneradmin")`, but their associated VmHostSlice records were still being monitored. This is unnecessary since runners have their own monitoring entry via GithubRunner. Filter them out with a subquery on the vm table.

title: Upgrade rubocop-capybara to 2.22.1
description:
rubocop-capybara 2.21.0 is incompatible with rubocop 1.84.2, crashing with "Passing a project root directory to inject_defaults! is no longer supported."

Remove the < 2.22 pin that was added to work around Capybara/FindAllFirst issues (rubocop/rubocop-capybara#150). The upstream issue is marked as resolved, but the auto-corrected rewrites still break our tests, so disable FindAllFirst instead.

Also disable the new NegationMatcherAfterVisit cop which flags legitimate test patterns.

title: Fix missing bcc keyword
Wait for kubelet CSR before approving it during node provisioning
description:
The metrics server requires manually approving the kubelet-serving CSR whenever a new node joins the cluster. The previous code ran the approval immediately after installing the CNI, but sometimes the kubelet had not yet created the CSR by that point, causing the approval to silently do nothing.

The label now checks whether the CSR is already approved first, skipping approval entirely on retries. If not yet approved, it looks for a pending CSR and approves it. If neither exists, it naps to wait for the kubelet to create one.

title: Configure admin url for use by model/page.rb
description: Our alerts are currently linking to non-existant pages on admin.ubicloud.com

title: Add configurable days parameter to VM by IPv4 lookup
description: The archived VM query joins two archived_record tables and can be slow for large time ranges. With a 30-second web request timeout, the previous hardcoded 15-day window would sometimes fail to complete. Default to 5 days, which covers most abuse report investigations, while allowing operators to increase up to 15 days when needed.

title: Override rollup to fix security vulnerability
Remove Page.active dataset scope
description: Pages are destroyed on resolve since 388de89fa67, so every row in the table has resolved_at IS NULL. The .active scope filtered on that column but was effectively a no-op, adding noise without value.

title: Add a general zero-rate inference billing rate
description: For the cases where we handle billing out-of-band and fast-changing models, add a general zero-rate billing rate to be used within InferenceRouterModels.

title: Rename destroy label to finish in e2e test progs
description:
The destroy label in test progs is not a true destroy: it cleans up the test project and pops in the happy path, but not for failed case. Its failure path (hop to failed, then nap) did not match the expected terminal semantics of a real destroy label. Naming it "destroy" caused the framework to reserve a destroy semaphore that was never used

When hop_destroy is called, it also increments the destroying semaphore,
but it never decrements it when it fails and naps forever. It blocks to
destroy strand.

Rename it to "finish" to avoid the special-cased destroy semantics and
remove the unnecessary semaphore declarations.
